body: Yes on War of the Ghosts. The repository has an admitted real 1901 source text with named narrator and provenance, plus a researcher-reviewed hand-modeled narrative acceptance fixture. That should become the coherent end-to-end thread: actual lines of the story, exact spans, contexts and open hypotheses, recall alignment output, and plots whose values come from archived executable output. On Autobiographical Interview data, the current BirthdayInterview fixture is explicitly synthetic and invented. The admission checklist currently lists no participant transcript at all and bars participant recall text until the owner records a redistribution and REB or IRB basis; pseudonymization alone is not permission. I can show the synthetic interview transparently now, but I will not label it real. A real AI example needs a separate admitted dataset and consent basis before it enters the site.
